The Lighthouse Keeper

The keeper climbed the spiral stair every evening at dusk. The lamp had to be lit before the last light left the water, or the boats would lose their bearing against the rocks that guarded the narrow channel.

For thirty years he kept the same routine. Oil, wick, glass, flame. The sea changed its mood with the seasons, but the light did not. Sailors a mile offshore knew the harbour was still watched, still tended, still alive each night the beam swept across the dark.

When the electric light arrived, the keeper stayed on for a time to tend the machine that had replaced his hands. Then one spring he packed a single case, walked down the stair a final time, and left the door unlocked behind him for whoever might come next.
